text:
Rhea (Product): quick sync: we need a forward-looking routing roadmap that balances customer isolation asks with cost. customers request both predictable lanes and cheaper shared options. goal: propose MVP and launch criteria by next week
Omar (Eng): agree. high-level options: 1) dedicated lanes (per-tenant pools) 2) shared + deterministic priority/fallback 3) soft-slicing by token quota. each has different infra work and pricing implications
Tara (Arch): tradeoffs: dedicated = clear SLA but high utilization loss; shared+fallback = good utilization but needs strong observability and clear fallback semantics; soft-slice = cheap but risky for noisy neighbors
Priya (Sales): customers fall into two buckets: high-compliance (will pay for dedicated) and growth apps (want lower cost). sales needs a clear upgrade path and a one-page feature matrix
Liam (SRE): ops asks: per-tenant telemetry, eviction/rotation runbook, and cross-region failover playbook. also we need an automated way to drain traffic from a node without causing cache thrash
Rhea (Product): what would MVP for shared+fallback look like? what are non-negotiable launch criteria?
Omar (Eng): MVP proposal: - policy object per tenant (priority, region preferences, fallback chain) - fallback chain supports model-variant -> region -> capacity-tier - policy distribution + edge cache with TTL - perf guardrails: <=150ms median extra latency on fallback path
Tara (Arch): add: KV-cache affinity visibility per-tenant, deterministic eviction policy, and global circuit-breaker to avoid cascading fallbacks
Priya (Sales): include SLA tiers: Bronze (best-effort), Silver (priority routing), Gold (isolation-boost + SLA). need pricing uplift examples and migration ETA
Liam (SRE): canary requirements: traffic mirror to new routing for 10 customers at 5% for 2 weeks, automated rollback on increased fallback rate or latency regressions
Omar (Eng): infra decision: central policy eval vs edge-local eval. central is easier to iterate; edge-local reduces tail latency. proposal: central control plane + edge eval cache, consistent within 15s
Tara (Arch): agree on hybrid. add requirement: policy-as-config with versioning and clear rollback semantics. example config snippet for spike:
```
policy: {
  tenant_id: "cust-77",
  priority: "high",
  regions: ["eu-west-1","us-east-1"],
  fallbacks: ["lowq-model","secondary-region","dedicated-pool"],
  cache_affinity: true
}
```
Priya (Sales): timeline ask: sales needs private-beta availability by week 8. can engineering split milestones so we can promise that?
Omar (Eng): rough breakdown: spike (2w), core routing + policy engine (6w), edge cache + distribution (3w), tests & canaries (3w) -> ~14w total. private beta at wk8 possible if we scope beta to a smaller feature set and core customers
Rhea (Product): product acceptance checklist draft: 1) documented policy model & sales matrix 2) canary run without SLA regressions 3) migration playbook for 3 pilot tenants 4) telemetry dashboards and alerts
Liam (SRE): monitoring metrics: per-tenant p50/p95 latency, fallback rate, token cost delta, and cache hit-rate. alarm if fallback rate > 2% sustained
Tara (Arch): dependencies: model-variant registry API, per-tenant metadata in routing index, rollout automation, and cross-region KV routing tags. we should backlog missing items now
Priya (Sales): i'll prepare the one-pager SKU matrix and collect pilot customers. also request marketing copy around "graceful fallback" (avoid "eviction")
Omar (Eng): implementation notes: keep policy store versioned and immutable per rollout; use canary flags for policy changes; make sure rollout tooling supports quick rollback
Liam (SRE): ops-safety: enforce a global token rate cap per-tenant and per-region to prevent noisy-neighbor spikes from taking down a region
Rhea (Product): decisions: ship shared+fallback MVP first, with a clear paid upgrade path to dedicated lanes. owners: Omar (eng) spike, Tara (arch) design + migration pattern, Liam (sre) canary/runbooks, Priya (sales) pilot list
ci-bot: CI green: routing-prototype-spike tests passing (28/28) :white_check_mark:
Rhea (Product): next steps: Omar/Tara to run 2w spike and post results. Liam to draft canary plan. Priya to send pilot invites. we'll reconvene next Tue 11am
Omar (Eng): starting spike now. will post daily short updates in this thread
Tara (Arch): uploaded initial migration sketch to the design drive: https://rwd.internal/drive/routing-migration-sketch
Liam (SRE): scheduled staging failover test Thu 02:00 UTC. will share results here
Priya (Sales): sending pilot invites today. will confirm list by EOD
Rhea (Product): thanks team. add blockers here. end-of-thread recap: MVP scope = shared+fallback, hybrid policy plane, canary plan, beta wk8 (conditional). owners assigned. :thumbsup:
